Fit a time-dynamic mixed-effects model

tdmm.Rd

Fit Gaussian, Bernoulli, or Poisson longitudinal outcomes with time-varying coefficient functions and subject-specific random intercepts.

Usage

tdmm(data, family = c("gaussian", "bernoulli", "poisson"), nknots = NULL, subject.var = "subject.ID", 
    time.var = "time", y.var = "y", x.var = NULL, degree = 3, n.chains = 3, n.iter = 10000, n.burn = 3000, 
    n.thin = 5, n.adapt = 5000, jags.dir = NULL, quiet = FALSE, n_basis = NULL, control = NULL, priors = NULL)

Arguments

data

Long-format data frame: one row per observed subject and time.

family

One of "gaussian", "bernoulli", or "poisson".

nknots

Deprecated compatibility argument with its historical interval-count interpretation. Do not supply with n_basis.

subject.var

Name of the subject ID column.

time.var

Name of the numeric observation-time column.

y.var

Name of the response column.

x.var

Names of numeric covariates, in coefficient order; NULL selects all columns other than subject ID, time, and response.

degree

B-spline polynomial degree; default 3 (cubic).

n.chains

Legacy number of chains; prefer control.

n.iter

Legacy total iterations; prefer control.

n.burn

Legacy burn-in iterations; prefer control.

n.thin

Legacy thinning interval; prefer control.

n.adapt

Legacy adaptation iterations; prefer control.

jags.dir

Legacy model-directory override for compatibility; ordinary users should leave this NULL.

quiet

Suppress JAGS progress output when TRUE.

n_basis

Actual number of B-spline basis functions. Omission resolves to 8.

control

Optional list from tdmm_control() controlling chains, iterations, burn-in, thinning, adaptation, seed, parallel execution, and cores.

priors

Optional family-specific list, normally obtained from tdmm.priors(family) and modified by the user.

Details

Rows may have irregular subject-specific times and unequal visit counts. Numeric covariates may be constant or change within subject. Coefficient functions use an extended uniform B-spline basis with a second-order coefficient-difference penalty. The default is cubic with eight basis functions. Use tdmm_control(parallel = TRUE, cores = ...) for parallel chains. The coefficient functions are on the identity, logit, or log link scale for Gaussian, Bernoulli, or Poisson responses, respectively.

Value

A fitted object of class "tdmm" containing posterior samples, reconstructed coefficient functions, input metadata, variance summaries, and fitting settings.

See also

tdmm.control, tdmm.priors, summary.tdmm, plot.tdmm

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Requires JAGS and runs MCMC.
set.seed(42)
my_long_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(id) {
  time <- sort(runif(5))
  baseline <- rnorm(1)
  changing <- rnorm(5)
  data.frame(id = id, time = time, baseline = baseline,
             changing = changing,
             y = 0.5 + baseline * sin(2*pi*time) +
                 changing * (time - 0.5) + rnorm(5, sd = 0.3))
}))
fit <- tdmm(my_long_data, family = "gaussian", subject.var = "id",
            time.var = "time", y.var = "y", x.var = c("baseline", "changing"),
            control = tdmm_control(seed = 42))
summary(fit)
plot(fit)
} # }
